exercises.title: A stack on a slice
exercises.task: Read Stack: append to push, cut the last element to pop. Run traces the stack while it reads {[()]} and shows how each opener waits for its closer.

exercises.title: Back and Forward
exercises.task: A browser keeps two stacks: pages behind you, pages ahead of you. Visit is given. Write Back and Forward: each returns false when there is nowhere to go.
hints: Back: the current page goes onto the forward stack; the new current page comes off the back stack.
Forward is Back with the two stacks swapped.
Check b.back.Len() == 0 first and return false: popping an empty stack is the bug to avoid.

exercises.title: Balanced brackets
exercises.task: Before applying a JSON or HCL config, check its brackets. Balanced returns true, -1 when every ( [ { is closed in the right order, otherwise false and the position of the problem: a closer that does not match, or, at the end, the innermost opener left unclosed.
hints: Push the position of each opener; on a closer, pop and compare.
Three ways to fail: a closer with an empty stack, a closer of the wrong kind, openers left at the end.
Keep positions on the stack (not the characters): then the error position is right there, and s[pos] gives the character.
